content.title: Trump reaches deal with 9 drug companies to lower prices
content.description:
President Trump announced deals with nine major drug makers in a move to reduce pharmaceutical prices, granting a three-year break on trade tariffs if they invest more into US manufacturing. Market Domination Overtime host Jared Blikre breaks down the news.

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Domination Overtime.

content.title: Dow Jones' Merck, Other Drugmakers Strike Drug-Pricing Bargains With Trump
content.summary: Dow Jones stock Merck and eight other bellwether pharma companies struck drug-pricing agreements with the Trump administration on Friday.

content.title: Nine Drugmakers Strike Deals With Trump, With More to Come
content.summary: The most recent pledges mean 14 of the 17 drugmakers targeted by Trump this summer have agreed to lower prices for the Medicaid program for low-income and disabled people, sell discounted drugs directly to consumers and launch new medicines for the same prices in the US as they do abroad.  “American drug prices will come down fast and furious, and will soon be among the lowest in the developed world,” Trump said during an event in the Oval Office.

content.title: More Drugmakers Reach Deals With White House to Lower Prices
content.summary: The companies, including Bristol-Myers Squibb, GSK and Merck, would avoid potential U.S. tariffs in return.
